title: Sunny and the Tawny Frogmouth | Bedtime Story
description: Join Sonny the Quokka on a quiet evening walk through the Australian bush in this soothing bedtime story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales. Sunny discovers a tawny frogmouth resting perfectly still on a branch — and shares a long, peaceful moment of stillness with him.
narration:
The moon was soft and round tonight, resting just above the tree tops. Little Sonny the quokka wandered slowly through the bush, her paws making quiet little sounds on the cool earth. She was in no hurry. The night smelled like dry leaves and honey.

She stopped near an old gum tree. Something on the branch did not look quite like bark. She tilted her little head.

There — very still, very grey, with soft feathers the colour of the tree itself — was a tawny frogmouth. He sat perfectly still, eyes almost closed, his wide soft beak pointing gently at the sky.

Sunny held her breath. She did not want to startle him. She sat down quietly on the ground beneath the branch and watched.

For a long moment, nothing moved. The bush was still. Even the leaves seemed to pause.

Then, slowly — oh so slowly — the frogmouth opened one golden eye. Just one. He looked at Sunny. His eye was round and calm and full of a very old kind of peace.

Sunny smiled her softest smile.

The frogmouth closed his eye again. That was enough. It was a very complete hello.

Sunny sat with him a little longer, feeling still and quiet and full. Then she curled up at the base of the tree and let her own eyes close.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, tawny frogmouth. Goodnight, little one.
